shorts.hook: A Komodo dragon can smell you from four kilometers away.
shorts.title: A Komodo Dragon Can Smell Carrion Four Kilometers Away
shorts.outro: The dragon never looked behind the rock. It didn't need to. When Doug moved on, it followed him anyway. How far is in the full video below.
shorts.end_card: HOW LONG DID IT FOLLOW DOUG?
shorts.description: Doug runs for nearly an hour and hides behind a rock, but a Komodo dragon's forked tongue can pick up carrion from four kilometers off, and what happens next is in the full episode.

shorts.title: A Komodo Dragon Ate a 31-Kilogram Boar in 17 Minutes
shorts.outro: Then Doug offered it a picnic as a peace treaty. The dragon accepted. Not just the sandwiches. It's in the full video below.
shorts.end_card: WHAT ELSE DID THE DRAGON EAT?
shorts.description: Komodo dragons can eat up to 80 percent of their body weight in one sitting and then bask for days to digest it, and what the dragon took from Doug's peace-treaty picnic is in the full episode.

shorts.hook: A Komodo dragon had babies without ever meeting a male.
shorts.title: Komodo Dragons Can Have Babies Without Ever Meeting a Male
shorts.outro: Komodos have outwaited everything for about four million years. Doug tried to outwait one with a folding chair. It's linked below.
shorts.description: Two zoo females laid eggs with no male around, and genetic tests published in Nature showed each mother was the only parent, so find out how long Doug lasted waiting out a Komodo in the full episode.
